note: The full F barre built from the open E shape: chord-shapes with written frets and fingers show E fretted with the fingers F needs, then F as the full barre; a strum-along squeezes and releases it, then C to F with a bar to move. The key is the lesson, so moves holds only a tempo range; the fingering lives in the chord boxes, not the text.

exercise.title: The full F barre
exercise.why: The full F is the open E shape moved up one fret, with one finger lying across all six strings in place of the nut, so three fingers make the E you know and only the barre is new.

cells.text:
Press a chord box below to hear it. Fret E as the E box shows, with the fingers F needs, then slide the shape up one fret and add the barre the F box shows.
Pick the six strings of F one at a time, and fix only the one that buzzes.
_Stop and shake out your hand when it aches._

Press Play below to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}. Strum F once on beat 1, then loosen your grip for the rest of the bar without taking your fingers off the strings.
Practice until every string rings on beat 1.

Press Play below to start the metronome. After a bar of count-in, the lit box shows the chord to play. Strum down once on beat 1, then use the rest of the bar to move to the next chord.
If the full F comes late, keep your strumming hand going and catch the next beat 1.
